title: Winterize your house before freezing weather
dek: Protect outdoor water, exposed pipes, and heating access before a freeze. Use the right shutdown method and plan for absence or power loss.
metaDescription: Protect outdoor water, exposed pipes, and heating access before a freeze. Use the right shutdown method and plan for absence or power loss.

paragraphs: Before freezing weather, disconnect outdoor hoses, use the correct shutdown and drainage method for your outdoor-water system, protect vulnerable pipes, and confirm the heating and emergency-contact plan. Use local forecasts and equipment instructions. No single temperature, faucet cover, or thermostat setting guarantees that every pipe is protected.

The urgent version is a cold forecast and a yard still connected for summer. Start with water and the ability to get help. Humidifier pads, fan direction, and general seasonal tidying do not have the same priority as an exposed supply line.

body.heading: Complete the freeze-priority pass
items: Identify outdoor taps, irrigation, and pipes in unheated or exposed areas.
Disconnect hoses and follow the system's instructions for draining outside lines.
Arrange the correct irrigation winterization method; do not treat closing one valve as proof the system is empty.
Address vulnerable pipe locations using suitable materials and qualified advice where needed.
Locate the customer-operated main water shutoff and confirm safe access.
Check that heating service and any known faults have been addressed.
Make an absence, power-loss, and emergency-contact plan.
Record what was done and anything still uncertain before the forecast event.

body.heading: Outdoor water needs the right method
paragraphs: The [Red Cross frozen-pipe guidance](https://www.redcross.org/get-help/how-to-prepare-for-emergencies/types-of-emergencies/winter-storm/frozen-pipes.html) recommends removing hoses and protecting outside water lines appropriately. Your faucet may have an interior isolation valve, a drain arrangement, or a different design. Confirm how yours works rather than forcing a valve or assuming an insulated cover drains the line.

Irrigation systems also differ. Some require a professional shutdown process involving components that can be damaged by incorrect handling. Do not improvise compressed-air pressure, connect a compressor without the right instructions, or assume the only requirement is owning the equipment.

body.heading: Choose work by exposure
rows: Hose attached to an outdoor faucet
Disconnect it and check the faucet's winter instructions.
Pipe in a cold garage or crawlspace
Identify exposure and obtain suitable protection advice.
Ask the installer or qualified service provider for the correct method.
Stop trying to operate it and arrange professional help.
Confirm the building, plumbing, and insurer's requirements in advance.

body.heading: Invented example: two days before a cold forecast
paragraphs: A homeowner sees freezing conditions forecast for Thursday. On Tuesday they identify the hose taps and find the irrigation instructions. One tap has a documented drain procedure; the other is unfamiliar. They complete only the understood work and contact a plumber about the uncertain line.

They arrange the irrigation service, confirm someone can check the property if heating fails, and write the unresolved tap question in the record. The example does not promise a ninety-minute job. The right outcome is completed protection or an explicit outstanding issue, not a universal checklist tick.

body.heading: Heating is part of the plan, not a guarantee
paragraphs: Follow equipment instructions and arrange necessary service before relying on it. The [CDC's winter guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/winter-weather/safety/stay-safe-during-after-a-winter-storm-safety.html) warns against using a cooking stove for home heating. Keep emergency arrangements appropriate to the people and equipment in the home.

For an absent home, ask a qualified professional and your insurer or property manager what is required. A familiar minimum thermostat number is not proof that a pipe inside a cold wall will stay warm. Plan for power failure, heating faults, access, and a person able to respond.

items.line: Which parts of this system need draining or protecting, and which valves should the occupant operate?
What winter shutdown method is appropriate for this installation, and what work will your visit include?
If the heat fails or water appears, who can enter safely, who do they call, and where is the confirmed water shutoff?

body.heading: If a pipe may already be frozen or has burst
paragraphs: Reduced or absent flow can require investigation. Do not use an open flame, and do not attempt inaccessible or uncertain thawing. Call a plumber when you cannot identify or safely deal with the problem. If water is escaping, use the confirmed customer shutoff only if it is safe to reach and operate.

Water near electricity, a bulging ceiling, a gas smell, or a smoke or CO alarm needs a safety response, not routine winterizing. Stay out of dangerous areas and use emergency or utility help. Do not enter standing water to reach a panel or valve.

body.heading: Keep the next year easier without repeating the date blindly
paragraphs: Record each system, method, completion date, and service provider. Next season, check the forecast and instructions again rather than waiting for the anniversary of last year's work. Climate and exposure make a fixed national deadline unhelpful.

For the wider season, use [fall maintenance planning](/guides/fall-home-maintenance-checklist). For finding and documenting the valve rather than guessing during a leak, use [the water shutoff guide](/guides/where-is-my-water-shutoff).

items.a: Complete relevant work before your property is exposed to freezing conditions, allowing time to resolve unknown systems and book help. Check local forecasts rather than using one calendar date. Pipe exposure, insulation, wind, and heating conditions make a single universal damage threshold unreliable.

Not necessarily. It does not automatically drain water left in the pipe or correct an unsuitable installation. Follow the faucet and plumbing system's instructions and ask a qualified person when the setup is unclear. Disconnect hoses as part of the appropriate preparation.

items.q: Can I leave the heating off while away?
items.a: Do not assume an unoccupied home can safely go without heat or other winter protection. The correct plan depends on the building, plumbing, climate, and applicable policy or management requirements. Arrange appropriate advice and a response plan before leaving.
